newsitem.title: USA: Indiana debt may have significant value - report.
newsitem.headline: Indiana debt may have significant value - report.

text.p: Indiana's strong fiscal performance, combined with continued trading of state debt at market premiums, suggests there may be "significant value" in Indiana state paper right now, PaineWebber Inc, a unit of PaineWebber Group Inc, said in a report issued Thursday.

"The state's combination of prudent fiscal management, a strong and diversifying economic base, modest debt levels and significant reserves provide investors with strong credit security," Municipal Research Director Michael Johnston wrote in the four-page report.

While Indiana has weaker-than-average resident income levels and a cyclical economic base, state general fund reserves far exceed those of other midwestern states and it carries a light debt load by virtually any measure, Johnston said.

Indiana unemployment rates have run below the national average for 10 years and strong fiscal management to address unfunded liabilities in the Teachers' Retirement Fund highlight the state's credit strengths, Johnston said.
Those steps include adopting legislation requiring a payroll setaside for new employees, establishing a pension stabilization fund and authorizing investment of pension assets in equities.
PaineWebber noted that while the outlook for a rating agency upgrade is uncertain over the near term, the longterm credit outlook is positive.
"Perhaps even more significantly, we believe that the state's current reserve levels provide a significant cushion against any future recessionary downturn," Johnston wrote.
Indiana carries no outstanding general obligation debt and funds most capital projects with lease appropriation bonds, PaineWebber noted.
